title: [EN - LinkedIn] Agents start more than 40% of GitHub pull requests
content:
GitHub published its Octoverse 2026 report
on October 28.
By September 2026,
more than 40% of pull requests on GitHub
started with an agent's 1st draft.
In March, that share was 17%.
GitHub counts 110 million of those pull requests
in September alone,
about 6 times the March volume.
Read that carefully.
This is GitHub's number,
and it counts detected agent 1st drafts.
It is not a count of every time
someone used autocomplete.

GitHub also says those pull requests
change multiple files about 87% of the time,
compared with about 79%
for pull requests without detected agent involvement.
By September, 90% of agent pull requests
merged within 2 weeks.
The comparison group held at about 86%.
So the work is not sitting in review forever.
It is landing.
That is why the review skill
is now the job, not a nice extra.

What does that mean if you want
an AI role this year?
Teams are not hiring
the person who can only type.
They are hiring the person
who can direct an agent
and reject a bad diff.
GitHub's own line is the job description.
Review is how developers shape what comes back.

Here are 3 drills for this week.
1. Each day, give an agent 1 real task
from a repo you already understand.
2. Read every changed line
before you accept it.
If you cannot explain the change,
do not merge it.
3. Write down 1 miss per day.
A wrong file, a missing test,
or a claim in the summary
that the diff does not do.
In 30 days you will have 30 misses,
and that list is your portfolio.

Say you are 2 years into a developer job.
Spend 1 hour a day on this,
on code your team already owns.
Do not invent a fake app for the camera.
The proof is a reviewed pull request
with your comments on it.

Here's my take.
The 40% figure is not a reason to panic,
and it is not a reason to stop reading code.
It is a reason to get faster at review
than the agent is at drafting.
The person who can check the work
is the person a team can trust
with the merge button.
That is the skill I would hire.

Follow for your daily AI update.
